title: Annual Accounts
summary: The ECB published its Annual Accounts for 2025, reporting a balance sheet of €603.3 billion (down €37.3 billion from the prior year) and a loss of €1,254 million. The balance sheet contraction reflects the Eurosystem ceasing reinvestments of principal payments from maturing securities under its asset purchase programmes. This is primarily an accounting document rather than a market-moving release.
key_points: ECB balance sheet contracted by €37.3 billion in 2025 to €603.3 billion, driven by non-reinvestment of APP principal maturities
Loss for 2025 was €1,254 million, significantly lower than 2024 due to reduced interest expense on net TARGET liability
Losses will remain on balance sheet to be offset against future profits, consistent with prior two years
Annual Accounts published 26 February 2026, representing year-end 2025 financial position
The document comprises management report, financial statements, auditor's report, and profit distribution note
This is an informational landing page linking to the full Annual Accounts and supporting materials
why_it_matters: This source provides the ECB's own financial position and is not a direct macro catalyst for markets. The balance sheet contraction reflects passive QT (quantitative tightening) from maturing securities rather than active policy changes. Loss figures indicate the ECB's financial stress from holding assets funded by higher-cost liabilities but do not directly affect monetary policy transmission or rate expectations.
macro_context: The ECB's financial losses and balance sheet contraction are consequences of the monetary policy normalization process. The decline in monetary policy securities reflects the winding down of APP reinvestments, a passive form of QT. However, this annual accounts document does not convey forward guidance or policy signals that would affect market expectations for euro area rates.
